steps.title: Log each result (due 5 business days after the reinvestigation ends); import a fresh weekly report and compare rounds.
Deleted items: confirm at all three bureaus and watch for reinsertion (written notice within 5 business days).
Verified items: ask how they were verified (15 days); send the furnisher a direct dispute with documents if not done.
No answer by day 30 after delivery (45 if extended): log the date and send a second dispute noting it.
Dispute again only with new information or a new, specific inaccuracy.
CFPB complaint for unresolved items, after the bureau dispute, written by you, once.
State attorney general complaint for unresolved items or collector conduct.
Keep evidence of harm (denial letters, rate quotes) for any inaccuracy a lender saw.
For documented inaccuracies that survived two rounds and were shared with a lender: talk to a NACA attorney or consider small claims.
Re-run the score estimate and add your actual scores.
Plan the next 90 days of score building (secured card or credit builder loan for thin files without other debt; authorized user from family; rent reporting where your lenders' scores count it).
If a mortgage is near, ask the lender about a rapid rescore.

steps.title: Answer 8 questions so these items can be disputed or set aside
steps.why: Some findings depend on facts only you know (did you apply, did a collector contact you first). Nothing is disputed until you confirm.

steps.title: Pay card balances down before each statement closes
steps.why: Utilization has no memory in classic FICO scores, so a lower reported balance can show on the next report. Statement balances are what issuers usually report. Plan: $2,200 across 2 card(s), overall use from 47% to 10%.

steps.title: Document-backed dispute: Late payments reported after the account was paid: EXAMPLE SECURED CARD 4000111122****
steps.why: The account shows a Date Paid of 03/15/2024, yet the payment history reports 30 days late in 05/2024, 60 days late in 06/2024 and 90 days late in 07/2024.

steps.title: Document-backed dispute: Delinquency jumps a step after a current month: EXAMPLE STATE CHILD SUPPORT OFFICE 7777****
steps.why: The payment history shows 08/2026 as current (OK) with $0 past due, then 60 days late in 09/2026. An account cannot be 60 days late one month after it was current (OK).

steps.title: Document-backed dispute: Same debt reported with a balance by the original creditor and a collector: NORTHWIND EXAMPLE BANK 5424**** and TEST RECEIVABLES LLC 8803****
steps.why: NORTHWIND EXAMPLE BANK reports a balance of $1,840 with the status "Charged Off", and TEST RECEIVABLES LLC reports a balance of $1,840 on the same debt, naming NORTHWIND EXAMPLE BANK as the original creditor. The same debt is counted twice; only one of them may report a balance.

steps.title: Document-backed dispute: Reported past the 7-year limit: OLD EXAMPLE RETAIL 6011****
steps.why: The report itself estimates this item would be removed in 12/2024, and it is still reported as of 10/20/2026.

steps.title: Document-backed dispute: Removal date later than the delinquency allows (re-aging): MIDTOWN EXAMPLE CARD 4111222233****
steps.why: The report estimates removal in 06/2030, seven years after 06/2023, but the delinquency began by 01/2021 (the first late entry in the payment history), 29 months earlier.

steps.title: Document-backed dispute: Sold or transferred account still shows a balance: NORTHWIND EXAMPLE BANK 5424****
steps.why: The account is marked "PROFIT AND LOSS WRITEOFF; TRANSFERRED TO RECOVERY" yet still reports a balance of $1,840. A sold or transferred account should report a $0 balance.

steps.title: Document-backed dispute: Maximum delinquency note disagrees with the payment grid: SAMPLE AUTO FINANCE 7310****
steps.why: The Maximum Delinquency Note reads "Maximum Delinquency of 60 days in 04/2022 for $410", and it does not match the payment history: the note names 04/2022, but the grid shows 30 for 04/2022; the note says the worst delinquency was 60 days, but the grid's worst rating is 30 days.

steps.title: Document-backed dispute: Removal date later than the delinquency allows (re-aging): TEST RECEIVABLES LLC 8803****
steps.why: The original creditor's account (NORTHWIND EXAMPLE BANK) is due to come off in 03/2031, but the collection by TEST RECEIVABLES LLC on the same debt is due to come off later, in 08/2032. A debt sale does not restart the reporting period.

steps.title: Document-backed dispute: Terms of $0 per month with amounts due: PAYLATER EXAMPLE INC PLA1****
steps.why: The terms read "$0 per month, paid Monthly for 12 months", but the payment history lists amounts due of $45 in 14 months from 08/2025 to 09/2026.

steps.title: Document-backed dispute: Terms of $0 per month with amounts due: PAYLATER EXAMPLE INC PLB2****
steps.why: The terms read "$0 per month, paid Monthly for 6 months", but the payment history lists amounts due of $30 in 8 months from 03/2026 to 10/2026.

steps.title: No new accounts and no closing cards until the loan closes
steps.why: A new account adds an inquiry and lowers average age; closing a card removes its limit from your utilization right away.

steps.title: Keep auto or mortgage rate shopping inside 14 days
steps.why: Newer FICO versions count mortgage, auto and student loan inquiries within 45 days as one; older versions use 14 days. 14 days is safe across versions. Credit card inquiries are never grouped.

steps.title: Know which scores lenders commonly use
steps.why: Auto lenders commonly use FICO Auto Scores; mortgage lenders commonly use FICO 2, 4 and 5, and VantageScore 4.0 is now accepted for loans sold to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Ask each lender which score it pulls.

steps.title: Pre-application checklist
steps.why: Proof of income (recent pay stubs or tax returns), your down payment in a bank account, and a preapproval from a credit union first so you have a rate to compare. If a mortgage is near, ask the lender about a rapid rescore after a correction or paydown.

blocks.text: I dispute the delinquency you report to the credit bureaus on my child support account EXAMPLE STATE CHILD SUPPORT OFFICE, account 7777****.
My child support case number is 0000000000.

A court order set the amount of my past-due child support and required periodic payments to reduce it, and I have paid on time every periodic payment for current and past-due support that the order required.
The account is reported with the pay status "Account 60 Days Past Due Date" and the payment history shows 60 days late in 09/2026.

Under 1 Tex. Admin. Code 55.102(b), past-due child support is reported as past due and zero months delinquent when a court order set periodic payments on the arrears and each payment the order required has been paid on time. Please report this account that way to every consumer reporting agency you report to, and report it as disputed while you review it (FCRA 623(a)(3), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2(a)(3)).

steps.title: Pull all three reports free at AnnualCreditReport.com (weekly is allowed) and import them.
Record any free scores you can see, with the model name, so the estimates can be checked.
If you had banking, insurance or utility denials, request your specialty reports (ChexSystems, Early Warning, LexisNexis, Innovis, NCTUE).
Freeze or add a fraud alert only if you suspect identity theft.
Pay revolving balances before each statement closing date; aim for low overall and per-card use.
Stop new applications; keep any loan shopping inside a 14-day window.
Optional: add Experian Boost (affects Experian-based scores only).
Log each result (due 5 business days after the reinvestigation ends); import a fresh weekly report and compare rounds.
Deleted items: confirm at all three bureaus and watch for reinsertion (written notice within 5 business days).
Verified items: ask how they were verified (15 days); send the furnisher a direct dispute with documents if not done.
No answer by day 30 after delivery (45 if extended): log the date and send a second dispute noting it.
Dispute again only with new information or a new, specific inaccuracy.
CFPB complaint for unresolved items, after the bureau dispute, written by you, once.
State attorney general complaint for unresolved items or collector conduct.
Keep evidence of harm (denial letters, rate quotes) for any inaccuracy a lender saw.
For documented inaccuracies that survived two rounds and were shared with a lender: talk to a NACA attorney or consider small claims.
Re-run the score estimate and add your actual scores.
Plan the next 90 days of score building (secured card or credit builder loan for thin files without other debt; authorized user from family; rent reporting where your lenders' scores count it).
If a mortgage is near, ask the lender about a rapid rescore.
